name: Review weekly memory score and seven indicators
description: Verifies the seven indicators, transparent 3-of-7 score coverage and the limitation that official product prices are not published weekly.
steps: Open Industry Cycle
Review all seven indicators
Inspect the score formula and normalized weights
Read the weekly data cadence notice
expected: All seven indicators are visible; only Server DDR5, HBM and NAND are scored; unavailable PC DDR5, DDR4, inventory days and company ASP are excluded; the score is 92/100 with 3-of-7 coverage and a note that price releases are monthly or quarterly.

name: Verify correctly labeled public DRAM and NAND references
description: Verifies government-published reference series retain their actual density labels and do not imply product-specific contract ASP.
steps: Open Product Pricing
Review DRAM 16Gb June to September 2026
Review DRAM 8Gb July to October 2026
Review NAND 128Gb June to October 2026
Check October values and unavailable DRAM 16Gb field
expected: DRAM 16Gb ends at September; DRAM 8Gb October is $27.5 per chip; NAND 128Gb October is $30.6 per chip; no October DRAM 16Gb value is interpolated and no series is labeled as Server DDR5 or PC DDR5 ASP.

name: Review annual and quarterly company actuals
description: Verifies annual actual series and latest released quarterly actuals for memory suppliers and AI supply-chain leaders.
steps: Open Company Financials
Review Samsung and SK hynix 1Q to 3Q 2026
Review Micron FY2026 FQ1 to FQ4
Review TSMC CY2023 to CY2025 and 2026 Q1 to Q3
Review NVIDIA FY2024 to FY2026 and FY2027 Q1 to Q3
expected: Annual and quarter actuals are visible in separate series; TSMC uses CY and TIFRS; NVIDIA and Micron use fiscal years and US GAAP; currencies and periods are not mixed.

name: Verify AI token, accelerator and memory demand series
covers: J.P. Morgan global AI token estimate
description: Checks the token-first AI demand page and its sourced translation into HBM, host DRAM and enterprise SSD demand.
steps: Open AI Demand and Data Centers
Review July 2026 token estimate and disclosed-floor/model range
Review input/output/reasoning/agent workload breakdown
Compare H100, H200, B200 and Rubin HBM specifications
Review KV cache sizing formula and caveats
Review HGX B200 host DRAM reference and inference SSD demand
expected: The page shows July 2026 token estimates as a range rather than an official census; agentic coding findings are scoped to the cited benchmark; HBM specifications are labeled as product maxima; KV cache formula includes model-architecture caveats; 1.5TB host DRAM is labeled as a minimum reference configuration rather than a market average; enterprise SSD demand is presented as a sourced trend, not a quantified shipment forecast.

name: Verify mobile navigation and chart readability
description: Checks that the current eight-tab dashboard is navigable on mobile and chart values remain legible with explicit units.
steps: Open the mobile menu
Navigate to AI Demand and Data Centers
Tap the 2026E AI token chart point
Verify the tooltip reads 400조 개/일
Scroll through low/base/high scenario charts
Open the Methodology page
expected: Navigation exposes eight current tabs and no removed Supply & Inventory tab; tapping the AI token point shows year and unit; chart title, tooltip, plot, x-axis and note do not overlap; tables remain horizontally scrollable.

name: Verify AI token history and semiconductor demand bridge
description: Checks token history and the traceable conversion from AI workload growth to semiconductor memory demand, with power-demand graphs removed.
steps: Open AI Demand and Data Centers
Review Jan-2024 to Jul-2026 token history
Review July 2026 disclosed floor, median and high estimate
Review training, inference, reasoning, agent and multimodal workload rows
Review HBM, KV cache, server DRAM and eSSD demand bridges
Review low/base/high scenario assumptions and forecast caveats
expected: Token history remains Jan-2024 through Jul-2026; disclosed floor, modeled median and high estimate are distinguished; workload types and memory conversion logic are visible; HBM product specifications and host DRAM reference configurations are sourced and labeled; no data-centre power-demand charts or power KPIs are present.

name: Verify AI token observations and semiconductor memory conversion
covers: OpenRouter observed tokens separated from global estimates
description: Checks that AI demand is token-centric, observed platform usage is not mislabeled as global demand, and public semiconductor memory configurations are separated from modeled market averages.
steps: Open AI Demand and Data Centers
Review OpenRouter monthly token observations and latest 7-day average caveat
Review input/output/reasoning/agent token workload table
Review HBM generation specifications and HGX Rubin NVL8 system-level HBM4 capacity
Review NVIDIA HGX host DRAM reference configurations
Review HBM, DDR5 and eSSD bit-demand formulas
Confirm no electricity-demand charts or PUE metrics are shown
expected: OpenRouter usage is labeled as a platform sample, not global usage; monthly averages and 7-day averages are not mixed; agentic coding benchmark findings are scoped to SWE-bench; HGX Rubin NVL8 shows 2 TB HBM4 and 130 TB/s system bandwidth; HGX B200/H200/H100 system DRAM reference is minimum 1.5 TB; HBM, DDR5 and eSSD calculations are separate; no data-center electricity demand charts are present.
